## Context
The RCA for grindable-deviant-angwantibo proved that any captured nested pytest without a private `--basetemp` joins pytest's user-global numbered root and synchronously performs unrelated stale-tree cleanup at session finish. The original helper is fixed in that ticket, but the required construct sweep found five semantically confirmed sibling launch sites outside its caller path.

## Confirmed sibling sites
- tests/unit/test_git_version_floor.py:163-177
- tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:830-844
- tests/unit/test_engine_dir.py:183-204
- tests/unit/test_scripts_import_convention.py:154-178
- tests/unit/test_tests_import_convention.py:92-116

The already-safe precedents are tests/unit/test_external_isolation.py:64-76 and tests/unit/test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py:14-25, which pass a private basetemp derived from parent-owned temporary state.

## Plan
- Inventory every live nested pytest subprocess and classify whether it already owns a private basetemp.
- Give each confirmed sibling a unique parent-owned basetemp without changing its entrypoint, cwd, marker selection, or child assertions.
- Add behavior-level regression coverage using an isolated cleanup-eligible `PYTEST_DEBUG_TEMPROOT`; avoid timing and source-text oracles.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every live nested pytest subprocess owns a unique parent-scoped basetemp or has a cited reason shared retention is required.
- [ ] A real-subprocess test proves cleanup-eligible shared numbered-tree sentinels remain byte-for-byte untouched.
- [ ] Existing entrypoint/cwd/selection contracts for all five sibling tests still pass.
- [ ] The default unit suite and lint/typecheck gates pass.
compiled_state.title: Nested pytest meta-tests still clean the user-global numbered temp root
